steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Each night, Elias climbed the spiral stairs of the Wit’s End Lighthouse to light its great Fresnel lens. The wind off the jagged coastline shrieked like a mourning gull, and the sea foamed against black rocks below. For twenty years Elias had tended this lonely sentinel—long enough that each creak of timber felt like an old friend’s greeting.  

On the eve of autumn’s fiercest storm, he noticed something strange: a tiny lantern bobbing on the dark horizon, half a mile out to sea. No vessel should dare sail so close in gale. Still, the light pulse was steady—three brief flashes, then one long glow—repeating like a cautious Morse call. Elias felt a tug in his chest, as if the lamp signaled to him alone.  

When the rain began, he fought the wind to refuel the lamp and heft his binoculars. Through the sheets of spray he made out a weathered sloop, its mast listing, canvas torn. No answer came to his shouts, only the relentless roar of waves. Determined, he lowered the lighthouse’s small life boat and rowed toward the drifting craft, oars biting deep into swells that threatened to capsize him.  

By the time he reached the sloop’s rail, its lone sailor lay unconscious across the deck—young, with sea-salted hair plastered across a pale forehead. Elias hauled him aboard and guided the little vessel back to the lighthouse. Inside the warmth of the lantern room, he wrapped the man in blankets and fed him tea until color returned to his cheeks.  

When dawn came, the storm had broken. The rescued sailor stirred. His eyes held gratitude and wonder as he asked Elias why he had risked his life for a stranger. Elias smiled and tapped the great lamp behind him. “This tower has saved countless ships,” he said quietly. “Tonight, it saved you.”  

As the young sailor departed on the morning tide, Elias watched from the top window. The Fresnel lens caught the sun and scattered it like a promise across the waves. The lighthouse stood vigilant—timeless, unyielding—and so did its keeper, ready to answer every flash and cry that darkness might send his way.
